neighbours.label: the token ' also' placed after its subject or at clause end in archaic or scriptural prose ('thy sins also shall', 'to the nations also'), as opposed to 'too', 'likewise' or 'as well' in the same frames
fire: And the elders of the city also shall stand at the gate.
Ye have heard my words, and ye also shall bear witness.
For the stranger that dwelleth among you, he also shall keep the feast.
Then came the women also, bringing spices to the tomb.
The Lord hath blessed thee, and thy house also shall prosper.
He sent his servants unto the villages also, to call the people.
Let the children also come, and forbid them not.
Our fathers trusted in thee, and we also will trust in thee.
